From 434ac4d51407ce3764a6ae96a89d90b8ae2826fb Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Colin Ian King <colin.king@canonical.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2020 16:24:28 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] remoteproc/mediatek: fix null pointer dereference on null scp
 pointer

Currently when pointer scp is null a dev_err is being called that
references the pointer which is the very thing we are trying to
avoid doing. Remove the extraneous error message to avoid this
issue.

Addresses-Coverity: ("Dereference after null check")
Fixes: 63c13d61eafe ("remoteproc/mediatek: add SCP support for mt8183")
Signed-off-by: Colin Ian King <colin.king@canonical.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20200918152428.27258-1-colin.king@canonical.com
Signed-off-by: Bjorn Andersson <bjorn.andersson@linaro.org>

diff --git a/drivers/remoteproc/mtk_scp_ipi.c b/drivers/remoteproc/mtk_scp_ipi.c
index 3d3d87210ef2..58d1d7e571d6 100644
--- a/drivers/remoteproc/mtk_scp_ipi.c
+++ b/drivers/remoteproc/mtk_scp_ipi.c
@@ -30,10 +30,8 @@ int scp_ipi_register(struct mtk_scp *scp,
 		     scp_ipi_handler_t handler,
 		     void *priv)
 {
-	if (!scp) {
-		dev_err(scp->dev, "scp device is not ready\n");
+	if (!scp)
 		return -EPROBE_DEFER;
-	}
 
 	if (WARN_ON(id >= SCP_IPI_MAX) || WARN_ON(handler == NULL))
 		return -EINVAL;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/remoteproc/mtk_scp_ipi.c`**
   - The code block that checks if the `scp` pointer is null has been modified. 
   - The line that logs an error message (`dev_err(scp->dev, "scp device is not ready\n");`) when `scp` is null has been removed.
   - The function now directly returns `-EPROBE_DEFER` if `scp` is null, without attempting to dereference `scp` for logging.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification addresses a bug where dereferencing a null pointer (`scp`) could lead to a null pointer dereference error. By removing the error logging that references `scp`, the patch prevents the potential crash that could occur when `scp` is null.
- The change improves the robustness of the code by ensuring that the function can safely handle the case where `scp` is not initialized, thus adhering to better error handling practices.

Here is the commit message:
remoteproc/mediatek: fix null pointer dereference on null scp
 pointer

Currently when pointer scp is null a dev_err is being called that
references the pointer which is the very thing we are trying to
avoid doing. Remove the extraneous error message to avoid this
issue.

Addresses-Coverity: ("Dereference after null check")
Fixes: 63c13d61eafe ("remoteproc/mediatek: add SCP support for mt8183")
Signed-off-by: Colin Ian King <colin.king@canonical.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20200918152428.27258-1-colin.king@canonical.com
Signed-off-by: Bjorn Andersson <bjorn.andersson@linaro.org>

Here is the root cause:
The bug is caused by dereferencing a null pointer (`scp`) when attempting to log an error message. The code attempts to access `scp->dev` to log the error, which leads to a null pointer dereference if `scp` is indeed null. This situation arises when the `scp` device is not ready, and the error handling was not properly checking for null before attempting to log the error.

Here is the patch:
  */
 int scp_ipi_register(struct mtk_scp *scp,
 		     u32 id,
 		     scp_ipi_handler_t handler,
 		     void *priv)
 {
-	if (!scp) {
-		dev_err(scp->dev, "scp device is not ready\n");
+	if (!scp)
 		return -EPROBE_DEFER;
-	}
 
 	if (WARN_ON(id >= SCP_IPI_MAX) || WARN_ON(handler == NULL))
 		return -EINVAL;
 
 	scp_ipi_lock(scp, id);
 	scp->ipi_desc[id].handler = handler;
 	scp->ipi_desc[id].priv = priv;
 	scp_ipi_unlock(scp, id);
 
 	return 0;
 }
 EXPORT_SYMBOL_GPL(scp_ipi_register);

Reason:
This line attempts to dereference the `scp` pointer to access `scp->dev` for logging an error message. If `scp` is null, this dereference will lead to a null pointer dereference, causing a crash.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (!scp)
    return -EPROBE_DEFER;
```
Reason:
This change removes the erroneous logging attempt when `scp` is null and instead returns an error code (`-EPROBE_DEFER`). This prevents the null pointer dereference by ensuring that no further operations are attempted on `scp` if it is null.
